limitations: The digital fly's controller is a reduced-order state machine. It simulates no neurons; its links to Virtual Fly Brain terms are labels, not mechanisms.
Model parameters were chosen for this simulator, not measured or fitted; a result describes the simulator with these values.
Flight is kinematic: no aerodynamics and no MuJoCo physics run in these experiments.
The arena is a box with primitive obstacles and a relative light proxy (not lux); odour, temperature, humidity, airflow and food are not simulated.

The second look was added after ECHO-02's published held-out results showed the fly overconfident on combined causes, so these conditions are not naive for it; its one parameter was set by a principle, never tuned on them (docs/PROJECT_ECHO.md). The perturbations are the experimenter's models of an impairment, a push, a turning surface, a sensor fault and an obstacle, applied by the simulator. procedure: Preregister the exact fly plan; the registry's receipt fixes when.
A person at a terminal (or, for the host's demonstration designs, the demonstration script) authorizes the plan once; the authorization binds the receipt and draws a random nonce.
Derive the seeds from SHA-256 of the receipt digest and the nonce, and refuse any this fly has already run.
Run every seed in both arms on the host-built arenas and stimuli of the protocol, counting the gate's refusals.
Simulate every run a second time and require each state hash and measurement.
Recompile and re-simulate again before registry admission, from committed code only.
